Track model

Source: R/TRACK.R
TRACK.Rd

TRACK() builds a track model from columns of coordinates, date-times and track ids. A track model is a list of keyed tables: tracks (one row per track, key .track) and fixes (one row per location, key .fix, ordered by date-time within track). Segments between consecutive fixes are derived on demand with track_segments(). Ids are 0-based, as in the mesh models of 'meshcore'.

TRACK(
  x,
  y,
  date,
  id,
  data = NULL,
  crs = NA_character_,
  longlat = NULL,
  segment = NULL,
  policy = c("error", "repair")
)

Arguments

x, y

coordinates

date

date-times (converted with as.POSIXct())

id

track ids (a single value is used for every fix)

data

optional data frame of other columns, one row per fix

crs

coordinate reference system, carried as a string

longlat

logical, are x and y longitude and latitude? See Details.

segment

"geodesic" or "planar", see Details

policy

"error" or "repair", see Details

Value

A track model: a list with meta, tracks and fixes, with class "TRACK".

Details

A fix is identified by its track and its date-time, not by its position: two fixes at the same coordinates are different fixes. This is recorded as rung = "sequential" in meta.

The rules are those of the 'trip' package: no missing values in the coordinates, date-times or ids, records ordered by date-time within track, no duplicated records, and no duplicated date-times within a track. policy = "error" stops when a rule is broken. policy = "repair" removes records with missing values, orders the records, removes duplicated records, and moves duplicated date-times forward by one second until they are unique, and records what it did in meta$log.

longlat says whether the coordinates are longitude and latitude, which decides how distances are measured. When it is NULL it is taken from crs: TRUE when crs is missing or names a longitude and latitude system, FALSE otherwise. segment says what the line between two fixes is: "geodesic" (the default for longitude and latitude) or "planar" (straight in the coordinate system, the default otherwise). track_cells() needs planar segments.

See also

as_track(), track_fixes(), track_segments(), track_cells()

Examples

tr <- TRACK(trips0$x, trips0$y, trips0$date, trips0$id)
tr
#> <TRACK> 1500 fixes in 3 tracks; segments geodesic (longitude, latitude)
head(track_segments(tr))
#>   .seg .track .fix0 .fix1       x0        y0       x1        y1
